name: Glyceregia
typical_results: Standard etchant for austenitic stainless steels and nickel alloys. The glycerol moderates the HCl-HNO₃ reaction rate, allowing controlled etching. Standard 3:2:1 ratio (HCl:glycerol:HNO₃) per ASTM E407.
preparation_notes: Add 5ml HNO₃ and 15ml HCl to 10ml glycerol slowly with stirring. Add acids to glycerol — not the reverse. CAUTION: Exothermic reaction. Prepare fresh — shelf life only hours.
application_notes: Immerse sample or swab for 10-30 seconds. Start with shorter times for nickel alloys. Rinse immediately with water, then ethanol. Dry with compressed air or warm air to avoid staining.
troubleshooting_notes: Prepare fresh for each use — decomposes within hours. Glycerol moderates the reaction. If insufficient contrast on Hastelloy, try Adler's Etchant. Use in fume hood.
storage_notes: Store component chemicals separately. Prepare fresh when needed — do not store mixed solution.

name: 2% Nital
typical_results: Reveals ferrite grain boundaries and pearlite colonies. Darkens pearlite, leaves ferrite light.
preparation_notes: Mix 2 ml concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃) with 98 ml ethanol (95% or absolute). Add acid to ethanol slowly with stirring. Store in glass bottle.
application_notes: Immerse sample for 5-15 seconds. Swab gently if needed. Rinse immediately with ethanol, then water. Dry with compressed air.
troubleshooting_notes: If over-etched (too dark), reduce time or concentration. If under-etched, increase time slightly. Ensure fresh etchant for best results.
storage_notes: Store in dark glass bottle with tight cap. Keep away from light. Shelf life: 3-6 months if properly stored.

name: ASTM No. 1
typical_results: ASTM standard general-purpose etchant. Similar to Nital but with variable concentration. Good for carbon and low-alloy steels.
preparation_notes: Mix 1-5ml concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃) with 100ml ethanol. Adjust concentration based on material hardness. Add acid to ethanol slowly with stirring.
application_notes: Immerse sample for 10-30 seconds. Adjust time based on concentration used. Rinse with ethanol then water. Dry with compressed air.
troubleshooting_notes: Start with lower concentration (1-2%) for softer steels. Increase concentration for harder materials. If over-etched, reduce concentration or time.
storage_notes: Store in dark glass bottle with tight cap. Keep away from light. Shelf life: 3-6 months if properly stored.

name: Chromic Acid (Electrolytic)
typical_results: Electrolytic etchant for stainless steels and nickel alloys. Good for revealing grain structure without over-etching.
preparation_notes: CAUTION: Chromic acid is highly toxic and carcinogenic. Dissolve 10g CrO₃ in 100ml distilled water. Use in fume hood with proper PPE.
application_notes: Use as electrolyte with stainless steel cathode. Apply 6V DC, 0.1 A/cm² current density for 60-120 seconds. Sample is anode. Rinse thoroughly with water after etching.
troubleshooting_notes: CAUTION: Chromic acid is a known carcinogen. Use only in fume hood with full PPE. Ensure good electrical contact. If no etching, check connections.
storage_notes: Store in glass bottle with tight cap. Label clearly as toxic and carcinogenic. Shelf life: several months.

name: Winsteard's Reagent
typical_results: For chromium steels and stainless steels.
preparation_notes: Dissolve 5g CuCl₂ in 100ml HCl, then add 100ml ethanol.
application_notes: Immerse sample for 30-60 seconds. Rinse with water and ethanol.
troubleshooting_notes: Similar to other copper chloride based etchants.
storage_notes: Store in glass bottle. Shelf life: several months.

name: Modified Kroll's Reagent
typical_results: Less aggressive version of Kroll's reagent. Good for sensitive titanium microstructures.
color_effects: Alpha phase light, beta phase dark
preparation_notes: CAUTION: HF is extremely hazardous. Mix 1ml HF, 3ml HNO₃, and 100ml water in plastic container. Use fume hood and proper PPE.
application_notes: Swab sample for 5-15 seconds. Do not immerse. Rinse immediately with copious water.
troubleshooting_notes: HF causes severe burns. Always use in fume hood with proper PPE. Have calcium gluconate gel available. Less aggressive than standard Kroll's.
storage_notes: Store in plastic container. Label clearly. Extremely hazardous - follow safety protocols.

name: Weck's Reagent
reveals: Grain structure, dendritic segregation, orientation contrast
typical_results: Tint etchant for aluminum and nickel alloys. Deposits a thin Mn-oxide film of varying thickness that produces orientation-dependent interference colors under bright-field illumination. For aluminum: excellent for grain structure and dendritic segregation (2xxx and 5xxx series). For nickel alloys: same concentration (scale batch to 10g/2.5g/250ml for larger samples) reveals grain orientation contrast.
color_effects: Orientation-dependent interference colors under bright-field; grain boundaries and dendrite arms appear in contrasting colors
preparation_notes: Dissolve 1g NaOH in 100ml distilled water, then add 4g KMnO₄ and stir until dissolved. Solution should be dark purple. Prepare fresh for best results.
application_notes: Immerse sample for 10-20 seconds. Check under microscope. Re-immerse in 5-second increments if more contrast is needed. Rinse with water, then ethanol. Dry with warm air. View under bright-field illumination for interference colors.
troubleshooting_notes: If colors are too faint, increase immersion time. If surface is uniformly dark or stained, reduce time or prepare fresh solution. Sample must be well-polished with no residual deformation for best tint results. Colloidal silica final polish recommended.
storage_notes: Store in glass or plastic bottle. Solution degrades over days; prepare fresh for critical work. Discard if solution turns brown or loses its purple color.

name: Al-NaOH Etchant
typical_results: For aluminum alloys. Reveals grain structure.
preparation_notes: CAUTION: NaOH is caustic. Dissolve 10-20g NaOH in 100ml water. Use at 50°C.
application_notes: Immerse sample at 50°C for 30-60 seconds. Rinse immediately with water.
troubleshooting_notes: Use hot for better results. CAUTION: Caustic - use proper PPE.
storage_notes: Store in plastic container. Label clearly. Caustic hazard.

name: Boiling Phosphoric Acid
safety_notes: Use fume hood and face shield. Boiling concentrated acid — extreme burn hazard.
ppe_required: Face shield; acid-resistant gloves; lab coat; fume hood
typical_results: Standard chemical etchant for alumina (Al₂O₃). Preferentially attacks grain boundaries. High-purity alumina requires longer etch times (up to 2 hrs).
preparation_notes: Mix 15ml distilled water with 85ml concentrated H₃PO₄. Use borosilicate glassware. CAUTION: concentrated acid.
application_notes: Bring solution to a boil, immerse polished sample for 5 min to 2 hrs depending on alumina purity. Check under microscope periodically. High-purity alumina etches very slowly.
troubleshooting_notes: If grain boundaries not visible after 30 min try increasing etch time. If surface appears roughened reduce time. Solution may need replacement after multiple uses.
storage_notes: Store concentrated H₃PO₄ in original container. Etch solution can be reused several times.

name: Boiling Sulfuric Acid (Zirconia)
hazards: Severe burns from boiling acid. Violent exothermic reaction if mixed incorrectly.
safety_notes: ALWAYS add acid to water — never reverse. Use fume hood and face shield.
ppe_required: Face shield; acid-resistant gloves; lab coat; fume hood
typical_results: Standard chemical etchant for zirconia (ZrO₂). Reveals grain boundaries and stabilizer-rich phases.
preparation_notes: ALWAYS add 50ml H₂SO₄ slowly to 50ml distilled water — never reverse. Use borosilicate glassware. Extremely exothermic mixing.
application_notes: Bring diluted solution to a boil, immerse sample for 1–5 min. Check under microscope. Repeat if needed.
troubleshooting_notes: If no etching after 5 min check that solution is actually boiling. ZrO₂ is resistant — patience required.
storage_notes: Store concentrated H₂SO₄ in original container. Diluted solution can be reused.

name: Molten KOH (Silicon Nitride)
hazards: Severe alkali burns from molten KOH
safety_notes: Molten alkali — extreme burn hazard. Use tongs and heat-resistant gloves.
ppe_required: Heat-resistant gloves; face shield; lab coat; tongs
typical_results: Standard molten salt etchant for silicon nitride. Preferentially dissolves glassy intergranular phase. Etching rate depends on sintering aid composition.
preparation_notes: Melt KOH pellets in a platinum or nickel crucible. CAUTION: molten alkali is extremely corrosive.
application_notes: Immerse polished sample in molten KOH for seconds to minutes. Monitor carefully — etching can be very rapid. Y₂O₃-containing grades etch faster.
troubleshooting_notes: If over-etched (grains falling out) reduce time drastically. Start with seconds. If no etching try longer immersion or confirm KOH is fully molten.
storage_notes: KOH pellets absorb moisture — store in sealed container. Crucible can be reused after cleaning.

name: Molten Na/K Bicarbonate (SiC)
safety_notes: Molten salt — extreme burn hazard. Platinum crucible required.
ppe_required: Heat-resistant gloves; face shield; lab coat; tongs
typical_results: Standard molten salt etchant for silicon carbide. Preferentially attacks SiC grain boundaries. Reveals grain structure and polytypes.
preparation_notes: Melt NaHCO₃ or KHCO₃ in a PLATINUM crucible. Molten carbonates attack glass and most metals. CAUTION: molten salt.
application_notes: Immerse polished sample in molten salt for approximately 10 min. Cool then dissolve residual salt with warm water. Rinse with ethanol.
troubleshooting_notes: If grain boundaries not visible try increasing time. If surface is heavily pitted reduce time. Ensure salt is fully molten before immersion.
storage_notes: Store NaHCO₃/KHCO₃ powder in sealed container to prevent moisture absorption.

name: Weck's Copper Tint
reveals: Grain orientation, solidification structure, dendritic segregation
typical_results: Tint etchant for copper and copper alloys. Deposits a thin MnO₂ film whose thickness varies with crystallographic orientation, producing interference colors under bright-field illumination. Distinct from the aluminum Weck's formulation (4g/1g/100ml). Excellent for revealing grain orientation contrast, dendritic patterns, and segregation in cast copper alloys.
color_effects: Orientation-dependent interference colors under bright-field; grains appear in contrasting colors
preparation_notes: Dissolve 5g NaOH in 250ml distilled water, then add 12.5g KMnO₄ and stir until dissolved. Solution should be dark purple. NOTE: This is a higher concentration than the aluminum Weck's formulation (4g/1g/100ml).
application_notes: Immerse sample for 10-20 seconds. Check under microscope. Re-immerse in 5-second increments if more contrast is needed. Rinse with water then ethanol. View under bright-field for interference colors.
troubleshooting_notes: If colors are too faint increase immersion time. If surface is uniformly dark reduce time or prepare fresh solution. Sample must be well-polished with colloidal silica final polish for best tint results. If no colors appear the surface may have residual deformation — re-polish.
storage_notes: Store in glass or plastic bottle. Solution degrades over days; prepare fresh for critical work. Discard if solution turns brown.

name: Lactic-Nitric-HF Boride Etchant
hazards: Contains HF — extreme hazard. Deep tissue burns.
safety_notes: EXTREME HAZARD: Contains HF. Use HF-rated gloves and calcium gluconate gel must be available. Fume hood mandatory.
ppe_required: HF-rated neoprene gloves; face shield; lab coat; fume hood; calcium gluconate gel
typical_results: Etchant for boride ceramics including ZrB₂ and TiB₂. Reveals grain boundaries and secondary phases.
preparation_notes: EXTREME HAZARD: Contains HF. Mix 30ml lactic acid with 10ml HNO₃ then carefully add 10ml HF in a fume hood. Use plastic containers only.
application_notes: Immerse sample for seconds to minutes. Check progress frequently — start with very short times. Rinse immediately with copious water.
troubleshooting_notes: If over-etched reduce time. Start with 5–10 seconds. Boride ceramics can etch quickly in this solution.
storage_notes: Cannot be stored long-term. Prepare fresh. EXTREME HF HAZARD — follow all HF safety protocols.
